brief:
The person tagged the bot in a reply. The post they tagged it in says:
@buildthis.bisks.net make a site that purrs with synthesized audio. controls are cat size, room temp, cat mood. i trust your judgment on the algos, make it realistic but also fun.

The thread it's replying to, oldest first (this is the context "this" refers to):
@shimmermathlabs.com: this is a fun drone thing
my favorite setting

valence 3%
arousal 5%
dominance 93%

i prerecorded a bit in case the algo changes, but live link:
vadrone.bisks.net?v=0.03&a=0.0...

(headphones with good bass recommended)
  [quoting @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com: @buildthis.bisks.net An ambient music generator in the style of Brian Eno's "Music for Airports" but that uses a triangle slider for the dimensions of Valence–Arousal–Dominance (VAD) that shapes the generated tones and frequencies, with a "Play" button]
  [video, alt text: website showing 5 colors circles pulsing bigger and smaller as chimes play, low bass hums, and noise ebbs and flows.]
@words.bsky.social: the drone wormhole from this to the code for airport to mutual engine thing is glorious 

i heart bespoke vibecoded data sonification experiments
note: built purrbox: three sliders (cat size, room temp, cat mood) drive a Web Audio purr modeled on the real ~25Hz laryngeal pulse — cold cats shiver, hot cats pant, grumpy cats growl, ecstatic cats trill.
